title: Power Platform: Dataverse audit events sent to Purview no longer carry before-and-after values
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents the removal of field values from Purview-bound events and the need to update dependent monitoring. The control paths, API calls and permissions are supported, and the briefing distinguishes the conflicting published dates and the absence of change-specific licensing information.

claims.claim: Environment audit settings are at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings.
claims.quote: Select Manage in the navigation pane. In the Manage pane, select Environments, and then select an environment. Select Settings. Expand Audit and logs and then select Audit settings.

claims.claim: The printed v9.2 GET organizations call retrieves the five named organization auditing settings.
claims.quote:
Use the following queries to retrieve your organization settings.
GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations?$select=
auditsettings,
isauditenabled,
auditretentionperiodv2,
isuseraccessauditenabled,
useraccessauditinginterval HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: Changing auditing settings requires the System Administrator or System Customizer role or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: You must have a system administrator or system customizer role or equivalent permissions to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Dataverse user access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.
claims.quote: User access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.

claims.claim: The documented app route is Settings > Advanced Settings > System > Auditing > Audit Summary view.
claims.quote: From the app, select the Settings icon on the banner, select Advanced Settings, and then select System > Auditing > Audit Summary view.

claims.where: Governance controls: Enable SAS Logging in Purview path
claims.claim: Enable SAS Logging in Purview is under Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy and Security > Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings.
claims.quote: Expand the Product list and select Privacy and Security. In the Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings section, toggle the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting to On.

claims.where: Governance controls: Enable SAS Logging in Purview explanation
claims.claim: Enable SAS Logging in Purview gives Purview access to each configured production environment's activity logs.
claims.quote: turn on the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting for each Power Platform production environment so Microsoft Purview auditing solutions can access the environment's activity logs.

claims.claim: The Learn notice describes no opt-in or opt-out for the field-value removal.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse Purview before-and-after field change values restore opt-out disable removal'; opened the removal notice, Manage Dataverse auditing, Configure auditing and activity-logs-overview. No opt-in or opt-out for the removal is described.

claims.claim: The documented auditing, audit-retrieval and SAS-logging controls do not provide a documented way to restore removed field values to Purview.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse Purview before-and-after field change values restore opt-out disable removal'; read the removal notice, Manage Dataverse auditing, Configure auditing, Retrieve audit data and activity-logs-overview. No restoration control is documented.

claims.claim: The Purview customer-engagement schema describes Fields as holding created or updated values.

claims.claim: Dataverse Audit History can answer who changed a field and what its previous value was.
claims.quote: Audit History helps users understand the update history of a single record. It answers questions such as "When was this record created and by whom?", "Who changed a particular field and what was the previous value?", or "Who shared the record with another user?"

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft says removing field-level values reduces the risk of exposing sensitive business or personal information through downstream systems.
claims.quote: Removing detailed field-level values from Purview-bound audit events reduces the risk of exposing sensitive business or personal information through downstream monitoring or analytics systems.
